NFL DFS Quarterback Rankings: Week 8 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, November 1 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 31, 10:43 AM ET

Josh Allen is the top-projected quarterback on the Week 8 DraftKings main slate at 22.8 DraftKings points for $7,700, against Baltimore. Dak Prescott (21.6, $6,300) and Joe Burrow (21.0, $7,000) are next.

Justin Herbert returns the most per dollar among quarterbacks projected for at least 15 points: 3.44 projected points per $1,000 at $5,000.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 31, 10:43 AM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Quarterbacks to know in Week 8

Josh Allen, BUF vs BAL ($7,700)

Josh Allen carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 22.8 DraftKings points at $7,700, the 3rd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.2 points clear of Dak Prescott. The model includes 6.7 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 2.97 projected points per $1,000, 12th of 19 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Allen averaged 22.9 points with a simulated floor of 9.2 and a ceiling of 42.1, and he holds 9% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Buffalo is a 3-point favorite at home against Baltimore, with an implied team total of 28.75 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Dak Prescott, DAL vs ARI ($6,300)

Dak Prescott projects 2nd at the position with 21.6 DraftKings points at $6,300. The salary works out to 3.43 projected points per $1,000, 2nd of 19 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Prescott averaged 21.7 points with a simulated floor of 8.9 and a ceiling of 39.4, and he holds 18% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Dallas is a 7-point favorite at home against Arizona, with an implied team total of 30.75 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Value: Justin Herbert, LAC at LAR ($5,000)

Justin Herbert projects for 17.2 DraftKings points at $5,000, which works out to 3.44 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 19 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. The model includes 4.2 rushing attempts. Across 10,000 simulations Herbert averaged 17.2 points with a simulated floor of 6.8 and a ceiling of 31.2, and he holds 2% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Chargers are a 6.5-point underdog on the road against the Rams, with an implied team total of 19.5 in a game totaled at 45.5.
